name: Flashlight
listed_description: A fast, flexible machine learning library from Facebook AI Research written entirely in C++ and based on the ArrayFire tensor library.
reason: No numbers reachable. README (facebookresearch/flashlight, now flashlight/flashlight) says 'fast, flexible' and 'high-performance defaults' via ArrayFire JIT but has no benchmark, no benchmarks folder (root: bindings, cmake, docs, flashlight, scripts), docs/source lists no performance page. The ICML 2022 paper (Kahn et al., 'Flashlight: Enabling Innovation in Tools for Machine Learning', arXiv 2201.12465) does compare Flashlight 0.3.1 with PyTorch 1.8 and TensorFlow 2.4 on six networks on V100-32GB GPUs in a DGX-1 (per search-result snippets, 'competing with and often outperforming'), so a paper-access retier could give a tier B record, but arxiv.org, ar5iv, proceedings.mlr.press, icml.cc, ai.meta.com, hgpu.org, liner.com and catalyzex are all EGRESS_BLOCKED here and no snippet carried numbers. MIT licence per GitHub (list tag says BSD-3-Clause), 5.5k stars, last commit 2026-10-06.

name: fft-c
listed_description: A high-performance Fourier Transform from netlib's fftpack; wrapped in a user-friendly format
reason: Directional claim only. README says 'FFTPACK is a very high-performance fft tool even when compared to Apple's vDSP and many other libraries' with no numbers, no benchmark, no timing harness (repo files: fft.c, fft.h, fft.doc, FFTPACK.txt, example.c, Makefile, LICENSE; example.c only prints the time axis of its demo signal, no durations). The claim is about upstream FFTPACK, which is a wrapper target here, and the better-known evidence (FFTW and PFFFT benchmarks) shows FFTPACK slower than FFTW, MKL and vDSP-class SIMD libraries, which contradicts the README's claim. MIT licence, 27 stars, last commit 2021-12-13.

name: fpsqrt
listed_description: Fast fixed point and floating point square root for C.
reason: No timing numbers anywhere reachable. README describes a 1993 shift-and-subtract fixed-point sqrt (sqrt_i32, sqrt_i64, sqrt_i32_to_fx16_16, sqrt_fx16_16_to_fx16_16) using only 32-bit add, subtract and shifts, and a 2023 overflow fix 'with a slight performance penalty' with no figure. main.c only checks correctness against libm sqrt over a range of values, no clock or benchmark; usenetPost.txt has no speed numbers; repo has 7 files (fpsqrt.c, fpsqrt.h, main.c, README.md, LICENSE, usenetPost.txt, .gitignore). MIT licence, 97 stars, last commit 2023-09-16.
